Forecast
fōr'kăst
v. (to scheme beforehand; in Daniel, to contrive devices against another)
English fore-, before, with cast, to throw or reckon — to cast up an account in advance. In Daniel 11 the sense is wholly hostile: to lay plans against a man.

Biblical Definition

The word occurs once, in the great prophecy of the kings of the north and south: “And he shall stir up his power and his courage against the king of the south with a great army; and the king of the south shall be stirred up to battle with a very great and mighty army; but he shall not stand: for they shall forecast devices against him” (Dan 11:25). The forecasting is not weather-watching but conspiracy; the king of the south falls not for want of soldiers but because men at his own table have cast up a plan against him. That is the point of the whole chapter, in which armies are raised and treaties made and none of it moves an inch outside what was written beforehand. Daniel is given the plans of men centuries in advance, which is the strongest possible statement of who actually forecasts. The LORD says it of Himself: “Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure” (Isa 46:10). Proverbs states the same truth in the compass of a household: “A man's heart deviseth his way: but the LORD directeth his steps” (Pro 16:9).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines to forecast as to foresee, to provide against, to scheme or plan before execution; and as a noun, foresight of consequences and provision against them.

expand to see more

FORECAST, v.t. To foresee; to provide against.

2. To scheme; to plan before execution. They shall forecast devices against him. Dan. xi.

FORECAST, v.i. To form a scheme previously; to contrive beforehand.

FORECAST, n. Foresight of consequences, and provision against them; previous contrivance.

Key Scripture

Dan 11:25 — "And he shall stir up his power and his courage against the king of the south with a great army; and the king of the south shall be stirred up to battle with a very great and mighty army; but he shall not stand: for they shall forecast devices against him."

Isa 46:10 — "Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure:"

Pro 16:9 — "A man's heart deviseth his way: but the LORD directeth his steps."

Psa 33:11 — "The counsel of the LORD standeth for ever, the thoughts of his heart to all generations."

Modern Corruption

Prediction has become the chief authority of public life, and men who cannot tell what shall be on the morrow speak of the future in the tone Isaiah 46:10 reserves for God.

expand to see more

There is nothing wrong with foresight; Scripture commends the ant, the prudent man who foreseeth the evil, and the builder who counts his cost. What Daniel names is different. To forecast devices against him is to use foresight as a weapon — to model another man's weaknesses and lay the plan that exploits them. The chapter shows it working at the level of empires, but the same faculty runs a family or a congregation, and the mark of it is that the planning is done about a person rather than with him. A man who finds himself rehearsing how a conversation must be steered, what must be withheld, and which allies must be secured first, has crossed from prudence into forecasting devices, whatever the cause he thinks he serves.

The second corruption is a whole civilisation's and it lives in the tone. Projections are issued about markets, populations, climates and the fortunes of nations in language of settled certainty, and the men who issue them are seldom held to account when the years arrive and disprove them. The Christian answer is not contempt for measurement, which is a good gift, but the recovery of the distinction Isaiah draws. God alone declares the end from the beginning, because He alone has decreed it; every other forecast is an estimate made from inside the thing being estimated. That is why James tells believers to say if the Lord will, and why Proverbs sets the two clauses side by side without any embarrassment — the man devises his way, and it is the LORD who directs his steps. Both are true, and the second governs the first.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew chashab (H2803), to reckon or devise, with machashabah (H4284), a device or plan; set against the LORD's etsah (H6098), counsel that stands.

expand to see more

Hebrew chashab (H2803) — to reckon, to contrive; rendered forecast where devices are laid against the king; Daniel 11:25.

Hebrew machashabah (H4284) — a device, a plan, a thought; the devices of the heathen brought to nought; Psalm 33:10.

Hebrew etsah (H6098) — counsel, purpose; the counsel of the LORD that standeth for ever; Psalm 33:11, Isaiah 46:10.

Hebrew kun (H3559) — to establish, to direct; the LORD directeth the steps of the man who devised his way; Proverbs 16:9.

Greek proginosko (G4267) — to know beforehand; the foreknowledge that belongs to God and not to the forecaster; Romans 8:29.

Usage

"“They shall forecast devices against him” — foresight turned into a weapon."

"“Declaring the end from the beginning” — the only forecasting that is certain."

"“A man's heart deviseth his way: but the LORD directeth his steps” — both true, and the second governs."
